section: Nehru era - foreign policy, planning, secularism, institution building
subsections: Five Year Plans (First to Third), Planning Commission and NDC
Foreign policy - Non-Alignment, Panchsheel, Bandung, Korea and Suez
Institution building - IITs, AIIMS, AEC, CSIR, UGC, Rabindra Bharati

accepted.s: The Planning Commission of India was established on which date?
accepted.x: The Planning Commission was set up on 15 March 1950 through an executive resolution.
accepted.tq: Direct date recall using closely related institutional dates as distractors.
accepted.sec: Five Year Plans (First to Third), Planning Commission and NDC  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Planning Commission:
1. It was established through an executive resolution.
2. It was a constitutional body.
3. Its establishment was linked to Article 39 of the Directive Principles of State Policy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Planning Commission was an executive, neither constitutional nor statutory, body. Its objectives were linked with Article 39 of the Directive Principles of State Policy.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong institutional-status statement and distinguish constitutional from executive bodies.
accepted.sec: Five Year Plans (First to Third), Planning Commission and NDC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following combinations is correct regarding the Planning Commission?
o: Jawaharlal Nehru—Chairman; Gulzarilal Nanda—first Deputy Chairman; M.S. Ahluwalia—last Deputy Chairman
Gulzarilal Nanda—Chairman; Jawaharlal Nehru—first Deputy Chairman; M.S. Ahluwalia—last Deputy Chairman
Jawaharlal Nehru—Chairman; M.S. Ahluwalia—first Deputy Chairman; Gulzarilal Nanda—last Deputy Chairman
M.S. Ahluwalia—Chairman; Jawaharlal Nehru—first Deputy Chairman; Gulzarilal Nanda—last Deputy Chairman
accepted.x: The Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, was the ex officio Chairman. Gulzarilal Nanda was the first Deputy Chairman and M.S. Ahluwalia was the last Deputy Chairman.
accepted.tq: Use the office-holder sequence and watch for swapped authorities.
accepted.sec: Five Year Plans (First to Third), Planning Commission and NDC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Planning Committee, constituted by the Congress in 1938, was headed by:
accepted.x: The Congress's National Planning Committee of 1938 was headed by Jawaharlal Nehru.
accepted.tq: Direct person–institution recall with neighbouring national leaders as distractors.
accepted.sec: Five Year Plans (First to Third), Planning Commission and NDC  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the National Development Council, consider the following statements:
1. It was set up on 6 August 1952.
2. It was chaired by the Prime Minister.
3. It gave final approval to Five Year Plans.
4. Its membership included all Chief Ministers, Union Cabinet Ministers, representatives of Union Territories and members of the Planning Commission.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly describe the date, chairmanship, composition and plan-approval role of the National Development Council.
accepted.tq: Test a complete institutional profile through an all-inclusive option.
accepted.sec: Five Year Plans (First to Third), Planning Commission and NDC  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Plan)
 a. First Five Year Plan
 b. Second Five Year Plan
 c. Third Five Year Plan
List-II (Model or description)
 i. Gadgil Yojana
 ii. Harrod-Domar model
 iii. P.C. Mahalanobis model

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The First Plan used the Harrod-Domar model, the Second Plan followed the P.C. Mahalanobis model, and the Third Plan was called the Gadgil Yojana.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure plan–model pair and eliminate the swapped codes.
accepted.sec: Five Year Plans (First to Third), Planning Commission and NDC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The First Five Year Plan was launched on 1 April 1951. Its principal priorities were:
o: Heavy industry, capital goods and urbanisation
accepted.x: The First Plan, launched on 1 April 1951, prioritised agriculture, irrigation and power, including projects such as Bhakra Nangal and Hirakud.
accepted.tq: Compare the sectoral priorities of successive plans rather than their names alone.
accepted.sec: Five Year Plans (First to Third), Planning Commission and NDC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the First Five Year Plan is correct?
o: Its actual growth was 3.6 per cent against a target of 2.1 per cent.
It recorded no measurable growth because it was confined to irrigation.
Its actual growth was 2.1 per cent against a target of 4.5 per cent.
Its target growth rate was 3.6 per cent and actual growth was 2.1 per cent.
accepted.x: The First Plan achieved 3.6 per cent growth against its target of 2.1 per cent.
accepted.tq: Separate target from achievement and avoid reversing the two figures.
accepted.sec: Five Year Plans (First to Third), Planning Commission and NDC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Second Five Year Plan is associated primarily with which of the following?
o: Village and cottage industries under a decentralised model
Food self-sufficiency under the Gadgil Yojana
Heavy and capital-goods industries under the P.C. Mahalanobis model
Agriculture and irrigation under the Harrod-Domar model
accepted.x: The Second Plan, covering 1956–61, followed the P.C. Mahalanobis or Nehru-Mahalanobis-Feldman model and gave priority to heavy and capital-goods industries.
accepted.tq: Direct plan–model–priority matching with closely related alternatives.
accepted.sec: Five Year Plans (First to Third), Planning Commission and NDC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A major consequence associated with the strategy of the Second Five Year Plan was:
o: Food shortages and inflation following the neglect of agriculture
Immediate food self-sufficiency and price stability
The replacement of central planning by annual plans
accepted.x: The Second Plan's emphasis on heavy industry neglected agriculture, contributing to food shortages and inflation.
accepted.tq: Apply the plan's sectoral imbalance to its stated outcome.
accepted.sec: Five Year Plans (First to Third), Planning Commission and NDC  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Third Five Year Plan:
1. It covered the period 1961–66.
2. It aimed at self-sufficiency in food.
3. Its guiding idea included growth with stability.
4. It was based on the John Sandy and S. Chakravarty model.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Third Plan ran from 1961 to 1966, used the John Sandy and S. Chakravarty model, and sought food self-sufficiency and growth with stability.
accepted.tq: Combine period, model and objectives in a full plan profile.
accepted.sec: Five Year Plans (First to Third), Planning Commission and NDC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Third Five Year Plan was derailed mainly by:
o: The Green Revolution and excess food production
The Suez Crisis and the Korean War
The abolition of the Planning Commission and the 1971 war
accepted.x: The Third Plan was adversely affected by the wars of 1962 and 1965 and by drought.
accepted.tq: Cause–effect recall using historically adjacent but unrelated crises as traps.
accepted.sec: Five Year Plans (First to Third), Planning Commission and NDC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the period immediately following the failure of the Third Five Year Plan?
o: A Plan Holiday from 1966 to 1969 with three annual plans, accompanied by rupee devaluation
A permanent suspension of planning from 1966 to 1971 without annual plans
A fourth Five Year Plan beginning immediately in 1966 without currency changes
A return to the First Plan model without any change in the rupee
accepted.x: The failure of the Third Plan led to the Plan Holiday of 1966–69, during which three annual plans were implemented and the rupee was devalued.
accepted.tq: Identify the transition period and distinguish annual plans from a regular Five Year Plan.
accepted.sec: Five Year Plans (First to Third), Planning Commission and NDC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Planning Commission was dissolved in 2014 and replaced by NITI Aayog in:
accepted.x: The Planning Commission was dissolved in 2014 and NITI Aayog replaced it in 2015.
accepted.tq: Separate the year of dissolution from the year of replacement.
accepted.sec: Five Year Plans (First to Third), Planning Commission and NDC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Jawaharlal Nehru set out the objective of keeping India independent of power blocs in a broadcast delivered on:
accepted.x: Nehru articulated the goal of staying independent of power blocs in his broadcast of 7 September 1946.
accepted.tq: Direct date recall from the evolution of non-alignment.
accepted.sec: Foreign policy - Non-Alignment, Panchsheel, Bandung, Korea and Suez  [other exams]

accepted.s: Panchsheel was stated in the preamble of the India-China Agreement on Trade and Intercourse with the Tibet Region, signed by Nehru and Zhou Enlai on:
accepted.x: The India-China agreement containing the Panchsheel principles was signed by Jawaharlal Nehru and Zhou Enlai on 29 April 1954.
accepted.tq: Match the agreement, leaders and date without confusing it with Bandung or Belgrade.
accepted.sec: Foreign policy - Non-Alignment, Panchsheel, Bandung, Korea and Suez  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT one of the five principles of Panchsheel?
o: Mutual respect for territorial integrity and sovereignty
Collective military defence against power blocs
accepted.x: The five principles included mutual respect for sovereignty, non-aggression, non-interference, equality and mutual benefit, and peaceful co-existence. Collective military defence against power blocs was not a Panchsheel principle.
accepted.tq: Find the non-member of a named five-item list.
accepted.sec: Foreign policy - Non-Alignment, Panchsheel, Bandung, Korea and Suez  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which country was the first outside the India-China pair to adopt Panchsheel in 1954?
accepted.x: Burma was the first country outside India and China to adopt Panchsheel in 1954.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among the Colombo Powers by identifying the specifically stated first adopter.
accepted.sec: Foreign policy - Non-Alignment, Panchsheel, Bandung, Korea and Suez  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Bandung Conference:
1. It was held in Indonesia in 1955.
2. It was sponsored by the Colombo Powers.
3. Panchsheel was absorbed into its Ten Principles.
4. The Colombo Powers included India, Indonesia, Burma, Ceylon and Pakistan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly describe the Bandung Conference, its sponsors and the incorporation of Panchsheel into its Ten Principles.
accepted.tq: Test the venue, year, sponsoring group and principle together.
accepted.sec: Foreign policy - Non-Alignment, Panchsheel, Bandung, Korea and Suez  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Non-Aligned Movement was formally established in 1961 at:
accepted.x: The Non-Aligned Movement was formalised in 1961 at Belgrade.
accepted.tq: Direct venue recall with other locations associated with non-alignment as distractors.
accepted.sec: Foreign policy - Non-Alignment, Panchsheel, Bandung, Korea and Suez  [other exams]

accepted.s: India's role in the Korean conflict included chairing the Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission, which dealt with:
o: Refugee settlement after the Suez Crisis
Border demarcation between India and China
accepted.x: The Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission handled prisoners of war, and India chaired it in 1953.
accepted.tq: Identify the function of an international body from the conflict context.
accepted.sec: Foreign policy - Non-Alignment, Panchsheel, Bandung, Korea and Suez  [other exams]

accepted.s: Who led India's role in the Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission during the Korean conflict?
accepted.x: The commission was led by General K.S. Thimayya.
accepted.tq: Direct person–mission association with prominent Nehru-era figures as traps.
accepted.sec: Foreign policy - Non-Alignment, Panchsheel, Bandung, Korea and Suez  [other exams]

accepted.s: India's response to the Suez Crisis of 1956 was to:
o: Remain neutral and refuse any United Nations role
Send troops to support the invasion
Support the Anglo-French-Israeli invasion and withdraw from the United Nations
Condemn the invasion and send troops to the UN Emergency Force
accepted.x: India condemned the Anglo-French-Israeli invasion during the Suez Crisis and sent troops to the UN Emergency Force.
accepted.tq: Test diplomatic position and action together, avoiding reversal of the response.
accepted.sec: Foreign policy - Non-Alignment, Panchsheel, Bandung, Korea and Suez  [other exams]

accepted.s: Jawaharlal Nehru served as Prime Minister of India from:
accepted.x: Nehru was Prime Minister from 15 August 1947 until his death on 27 May 1964.
accepted.tq: Use both endpoints of a tenure and distinguish office tenure from constitutional dates.
accepted.sec: Nehru - terms, books, influences, statements  [other exams]

accepted.s: At the time of his death in 1964, Nehru was in which term of office, counting the interim government and the elections of 1952, 1957 and 1962?
accepted.x: Counting the interim government and the elected governments formed after the 1952, 1957 and 1962 elections, Nehru was in his fourth term.
accepted.tq: Count the stated sequence rather than treating only elected governments as terms.
accepted.sec: Nehru - terms, books, influences, statements  [other exams]

accepted.s: Jawaharlal Nehru represented which constituency in Parliament?
accepted.x: Nehru's parliamentary seat was Phulpur, not Rae Bareli.
accepted.tq: Directly separate two easily confused constituency names.
accepted.sec: Nehru - terms, books, influences, statements  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Book)
 a. The Discovery of India
 b. Glimpses of World History
 c. An Autobiography
 d. Letters from a Father to His Daughter
List-II (Associated fact)
 i. Written in Ahmednagar Fort jail
 ii. A work by Nehru
 iii. A work by Nehru
 iv. A work by Nehru

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Discovery of India was written in Ahmednagar Fort jail. Glimpses of World History, An Autobiography and Letters from a Father to His Daughter are also books by Nehru.
accepted.tq: Start with the unique place association and then assign the remaining works.
accepted.sec: Nehru - terms, books, influences, statements  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT identified as an influence on Jawaharlal Nehru?
accepted.x: Nehru was influenced by Fabian socialism or socialism, British liberalism, Gandhi and Soviet planning. German nationalism was not identified as an influence.
accepted.tq: Find the outsider in a list of intellectual and political influences.
accepted.sec: Nehru - terms, books, influences, statements  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly contrasts Gandhi's and Nehru's economic approaches?
o: Gandhi favoured a decentralised village and cottage-industry economy, while Nehru favoured heavy industry, science and central planning.
Gandhi favoured heavy industry, while Nehru favoured only cottage industries.
Both favoured an exclusively decentralised cottage-industry economy.
Both rejected central planning and industrialisation.
accepted.x: Gandhi emphasised decentralised villages and cottage industries, whereas Nehru supported heavy industry, science and central planning.
accepted.tq: Test a paired comparison by matching each thinker with the correct economic orientation.
accepted.sec: Nehru - terms, books, influences, statements  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Liberation of Goa through Operation Vijay
B. Khrushchev-Bulganin visit to India
C. Dalai Lama flees to India
D. Chou En-lai's visit to India for border talks
accepted.x: The correct sequence is the 1955 Khrushchev-Bulganin visit, March 1959 Dalai Lama flight, April 1960 Chou En-lai visit and December 1961 liberation of Goa.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two middle events by year.
accepted.sec: Chronology of Nehru-era events; 1962 war  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Dalai Lama fled to India in:
accepted.x: The Dalai Lama fled to India in March 1959.
accepted.tq: Distinguish month-specific dates in the chronology of Nehru-era events.
accepted.sec: Chronology of Nehru-era events; 1962 war  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Chou En-lai's visit for border talks—April 1960
accepted.x: The India-China war took place in October–November 1962, not December 1963. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Check the date against the established chronology and identify the reversed year trap.
accepted.sec: Chronology of Nehru-era events; 1962 war  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following were causes of the India-China war of 1962?
1. Disputes over the McMahon Line and Aksai Chin
2. China's construction of a road through Aksai Chin
3. India's grant of asylum to the Dalai Lama
4. India's Forward Policy
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The war was associated with the McMahon Line and Aksai Chin disputes, China's road through Aksai Chin, asylum to the Dalai Lama and India's Forward Policy.
accepted.tq: Use the all-inclusive option after verifying each stated cause.
accepted.sec: Chronology of Nehru-era events; 1962 war  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the consequences of the 1962 India-China war:
1. A National Emergency was declared on 26 October 1962.
2. Defence Minister V.K. Krishna Menon resigned.
3. China declared a unilateral ceasefire on 21 November 1962.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the National Emergency was declared on 26 October, V.K. Krishna Menon resigned, and China announced a unilateral ceasefire on 21 November 1962.
accepted.tq: Verify dates and consequence statements before selecting the complete code.
accepted.sec: Chronology of Nehru-era events; 1962 war  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Atomic Energy Commission was established in 1948 under the leadership of:
accepted.x: The Atomic Energy Commission was established in 1948 under Homi J. Bhabha.
accepted.tq: Direct institution–year–person association with other Nehru-era figures as distractors.
accepted.sec: Institution building - IITs, AIIMS, AEC, CSIR, UGC, Rabindra Bharati  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following institutions was the first IIT, established in 1951?
accepted.x: IIT Kharagpur was the first IIT and was established in 1951.
accepted.tq: Test the superlative claim and year together.
accepted.sec: Institution building - IITs, AIIMS, AEC, CSIR, UGC, Rabindra Bharati  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the University Grants Commission:
1. It was set up in 1953.
2. It became a statutory body under the UGC Act, 1956.
3. It was established as a constitutional body in 1953.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The UGC was set up in 1953 and became statutory under the UGC Act, 1956. It was not a constitutional body.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the year of establishment from the year and nature of statutory recognition.
accepted.sec: Institution building - IITs, AIIMS, AEC, CSIR, UGC, Rabindra Bharati  [APPSC]

accepted.s: AIIMS, New Delhi, was established in 1956 under the:
accepted.x: AIIMS, New Delhi, was established in 1956 under the AIIMS Act.
accepted.tq: Match the institution with its specific establishing Act.
accepted.sec: Institution building - IITs, AIIMS, AEC, CSIR, UGC, Rabindra Bharati  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research was established in:
accepted.x: The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research, or CSIR, was established in 1942; its national laboratories expanded under Nehru.
accepted.tq: Direct year recall while separating CSIR from other institution-building dates.
accepted.sec: Institution building - IITs, AIIMS, AEC, CSIR, UGC, Rabindra Bharati  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Rabindra Bharati at Hyderabad was built to commemorate the birth centenary of Rabindranath Tagore and was inaugurated by Nehru on:
accepted.x: Rabindra Bharati, Hyderabad, was built for Tagore's birth centenary and was inaugurated by Jawaharlal Nehru on 11 October 1961.
accepted.tq: Combine purpose, place and inauguration date in a precise institutional recall question.
accepted.sec: Institution building - IITs, AIIMS, AEC, CSIR, UGC, Rabindra Bharati  [APPSC]
